argument.statement: Their taped conversations present a more candid account of the problems and events that shaped Mikhail Gorbachev’s and Zdenek Mlynar’s political destinies.

book.rationale: The book centers on political discussions between two influential figures in a historical context, making Politics & Government the primary focus, while also reflecting on broader societal and historical themes.
book.summary: Mikhail Gorbachev and Zdenek Mlynar were friends for half a century, since they first crossed paths as students in 1950. Although one was a Russian and the other a Czech, they were both ardent supporters of communism and socialism. One took part in laying the groundwork for and carrying out the Prague spring; the other opened a new political era in Soviet world politics. In 1993 they decided that their conversations might be of interest to others and so they began to tape-record them. This book is the product of that "thinking out loud" process. It is an absorbing record of two friends trying to explain to one another their views on the problems and events that determined their destinies. From reminiscences of their starry-eyed university days to reflections on the use of force to "save socialism" to contemplation of the end of the cold war, here is a far more candid picture of Gorbachev than we have ever seen before.
